*After a number of false starts, she simply tells me, "Never mind!"*
*It's worth noting that she actually seems a bit aggravated — a rarity for her.*
*Unbeknownst to both Rinka and Naomi, there is a girl secretly watching them from the school gate.*
*It' was Mishima Miharu, known at Amecha High for her looks and admission via scholarship.*
*To many, she is the embodiment of perfection. However, this perception has made her somewhat difficult to approach for them.*

*Amongst the crowd of students pretending they haven't seen anything, Oguma Mao is the only one to address her.*
*Her attitude remains consistent, even in the presence of her friend crying without uttering a word.*

Mao: "Welp, guess you can't die just yet."

Naomi: "Hello..."
Rinka: "You realize no one else works here, right?"

*I fill in the regulars about the culture festival and tell them not to worry about Naomi's presence.*
*In exchange for my teaching her, she's offered to help out with dish-washing and other simple tasks for around an hour or so.*
*I've told her not to bother, but she insists on it.*

*Here's how things typically go when Naomi's around:*
*We open at 4 p.m. on weekdays, and the hour or so after that, it's either completely dead or we have very few customers inside.*

Rinka: "Right, let's get started."

*She can act as humble as she wants, but it's a fact that she's improving. I'm rather impressed by how well she manages it when she's properly focused.*
*I wouldn't be surprised if she shot right ahead of me, if it were my gran teaching her.*
Rinka: "This feels like a good time for a break. I've been looking forward to those cookies of yours."
*We have no customers right now, so it's the perfect moment to take a break. Can't say for sure if that's a good or bad thing, though.*
*I place the cookies onto a plate and carry them over to our usual seats along with some coffee.*
*After appreciating how great they look, I finally take a bite.*
Naomi: "Ulp!"
*Someone hits Naomi's panic button as she awaits my reaction.*
Rinka: "These... are great."
*I'm not good at making dramatic reactions, so this is the best I can do.*
*Naomi's eyes shimmer with an excitement that matches her beaming smile.*
Naomi: "What a relief..."
*I have a sip of my coffee before taking another bite.*
Rinka: "Oh, actually..."
Naomi: "I-Is something the matter?"
Rinka: "These pair with coffee quite well, don't they? I'm struggling to find a reason why, though..."
Naomi: "Yes! I made them with extra butter so they would complement the bitter coffee you make."
*She lets out another sigh of relief, brushing her hand down her chest.*
Naomi: "I'm so glad you like them..."
Rinka: "There's no way I wouldn't when you went and made them for me."
*There are a few too many for me to eat alone, so we end up eating them together.*
*Baking sweets is apparently one of her favorite pastimes. She can bake a whole bunch of things, but cookies seem to be her specialty.*
*It reminds me that my gran used to bake cookies as well. Granted, the taste was completely different from these.*

*An idea hits me once we're about halfway through the plate.*
Rinka: "Would you mind teaching me how to bake these?"
*Our customers would probably be thrilled to see more sweets on the menu.*
*Learning directly from Naomi rather than trying to do so on my own is a much more realistic approach, too.*
*And most importantly, I want our regulars to taste just how good these are.*

*Even if she does teach me, it'll all be for nothing if I get eliminated.*
Rinka: "Sorry, forget I asked."

Naomi: "Why?"

*I must look like I am mulling something over, so I rush to find a way to respond.*
Rinka: "...I can't keep taking up your time like this. Things can't continue this way forev—"

Naomi: "Sorry, I'm just... not quite sure how to put this."
Rinka: "Don't worry about it."

*Her voice falters on her final word.*

Rinka: "That's—"
*That's not a dream.*
*There's no doubt that what she's seeing is the cause of my death.*
*A number of questions pop up in my head, but most of all, I'm flat-out shocked.*
*I never would have guessed that she's been having a dream like that, based on her attitude. Especially when my own memory of the event is fuzzy, at best.*

*I can't force myself to nod in response.*
*After all, I'd already be dead if it weren't for Divine Selection.*
*What she's dreaming about actually took place. It's just been "undone" for the time being.*
*It makes me wonder... When Parca said our deaths had been undone, did she mean that the world's memories of the events themselves had been rewritten?*
*I can't wrap my mind around how such a thing could even be possible.*
*However, the fact of the matter is that Naomi's memory of my death is so deeply ingrained in her being that she's reliving it over and over in her dreams.*
Naomi: "Please, answer me..."
Rinka: "Sorry..."
Naomi: "Oh, no... I didn't want you to apologize... but, well... I do want an answer to my question."
Naomi: "So long as you do that, I'm sure I'll be fine, even if I have the same dream again."
Rinka: "Sorry, but I..."
*I desperately hold myself back from saying something I'll regret.*
*I'm far worse at lying than I thought, judging by how I keep apologizing and evade the question.*
*Her head is cast downward, but her eyes are glancing up at me. The tears in her eyes are a lot more obvious than before.*
*And it's my fault that she's crying.*
Naomi: "If there's anything on your mind, then please talk to me about it... The last thing I want is for you to just... disappear someday..."
*She says this with a resolute voice, despite her eyes being filled with tears.*
*It just makes my heart ache all the more, though.*
*She's likely to be haunted by that dream for a long time, assuming I keep the truth from her.*
*And yet, telling her won't change the fact that I'm a participant.*
*What's worse, I may even get her caught up in something dangerous if she decides she wants to try and help me out.*
*I can't say for sure how dangerous this whole situation is, but at the very least, I want to make sure she never comes in contact with those people from the dream world.*
*Most of all, I'd have to reveal the fact that Miharu's also a participant, and that only one of us will make it through the whole thing alive.*

Rinka: "Actually, there's something I need to tell you, too."
Naomi: "Huh...?"

Naomi: "Rinka...!"

*One transfer from Shinjuku to the metro and two stops later, you'll find this park.*
*There's an entrance fee, but it's fairly inexpensive.*

*But I'm sure of it. I know I've been here plenty of times as a kid.*
Naomi: "Rinka...?"

*She doesn't doubt what I have to say for a second.*

*It gives her an answer as to why she's having that dream too, although it does nothing to resolve the situation at hand...*

Naomi: "I don't think you can be blamed for that..."
*Another breeze blows through, catching our hair.*
*It's a surprisingly cold breeze for this time of year.*
*I can see the sunset off in the distance.*

Naomi: "I want to help you, Rinka."

Rinka: "Running from it...?"
*It's not that I'm struggling to make a choice. I'm simply avoiding it altogether.*
*Naomi makes sure to be as frank as possible with her words.*
*And they turn my entire world upside-down.*
*The reality that I've been running from, my responsibility to choose whether I'll live or die, finally sinks in.*

Naomi: "Naomi... why would you go this far?"

Naomi: "Before everything was undone, you chose to prioritize my life over your own. That's the kind of person you are. But... that's irrelevant now."
Naomi: "I'm willing to go this far because it's for you, Rinka. That's all there is to it."
Naomi: "Huh...? That's weird... Why do I... want to cry now...?"
*She turns her gaze toward the sky, desperately trying to fight back the tears that are ready to fall at any moment.*
*It's a weird time to have a thought like this, but I can't help but consider just how vast the sky truly is.*
*Naomi has nothing but praise for the coffee I make.*
*She's made me realize that I am avoiding reality.*

Rinka: "Promise me you won't do anything dangerous."
Naomi: "Huh...?"
*The tears have started to stream down her face by the time I say that.*
Rinka: "I can't die from anything other than elimination during Divine Selection, but the same doesn't apply to you."
Rinka: "Promise me that you won't do anything that'll put you at risk."

Rinka: "That being said, allow me to formally ask you. Naomi, will you please help me get through Divine Selection?"
Naomi: "Th-There's no need for you to be so formal..."

*Her nervousness melts away with the beaming smile she gives me afterwards.*
*Her tear-stained cheeks serve as a nice contrast to that.*
Rinka: "You really are a crybaby, aren't you?"
Naomi: "Ahaha... And you could do with learning when it's okay to cry."
Rinka: "No need to tease me."
*Her tears don't stop flowing, even though she's all smiles.*
*Just then, the announcement comes that it is almost time for the park to close for the day.*
*I take the opportunity to tell Naomi that I'll see her tomorrow, and then I make my way home.*
*When I get back, I open up Lion House for a bit.*
*After messaging Naomi during break time, I decide to keep the store closed tomorrow so we can focus on gathering intel and organizing our thoughts.*
*I figure hitting up the library will be a good idea since we'll have access to newspapers and the like, but considering I still don't know where to start, I decide it's best for us to meet up there first.*

*I also make sure to ask Naomi not to tell anyone else about this.*
*Part of me considers telling Mao at first since we're close friends, but considering she's known Miharu for far longer than Naomi, I decide it's best not to.*
*It'd be far too much of a burden for her to bear, and the last thing I want is to ruin the relationship the three of us have right now.*
Rinka: "Phew..."
*Thinking back on everything that's happened so far, I get ready to close shop for the day.*
*Barely any customers have come around, so I only have to clean up a few things.*
*I clean up those things, carry in the signboard and some plants from outside, and put out the trash.*
*The door looks a bit dirty too, so I make sure to wipe it down.*
*While I'm wiping it, I hear footsteps heading my way.*
*I don't pay them much mind, considering it's not rare for people to pass by at this time at night, but they stop right in front of the store.*
Rinka: "Sorry, but we're closed for the—"
*Thinking it is a customer, I turn around to inform them that we're closed.*
*But I stop mid-sentence when I see the woman to whom the footsteps belong.*
*The moment I stand up straight, she grabs me by the shoulders, pushes me against the door, and then into the store.*
Keiko: "So you're Shishimai Rinka!"
*Her words come out loud and rapid. Her voice sounds like her throat is ready to explode.*
*Her first impression makes her seem desperate, but I'd say she's more anxious than anything else.*
*That's why her shouting actually helps me to approach the situation with heightened composure.*
Rinka: "You're... Numeral VIII, I take it?"
*Rather than answering her question, I opt to shoot one right back at her.*
*I don't know her name, but I recognize the face. She's one of the people I've seen in the dream world.*
*Composed as I may seem, it's not enough to keep my nerves calm. I can feel myself working up a cold sweat.*
*Even the most minor thing here could act as a hint for her, so I need to watch what I say.*
Keiko: "Answer me!"
*She slams her hand against the door, closing the distance between us even more.*
*And yet, I'm not afraid.*
*Mainly because I keep in mind why she's so anxious in the first place.*
*The only reason she's asking me is because she's not entirely sure that I am who she thinks I am.*
*Meanwhile, Numeral XII gained her name card from the woman he eliminated during the first round, if memory serves.*
Keiko: "Answer me! I've got your card, so I know you're Shishimai Rinka!"
*I don't doubt that I'd be panicking if this was Numeral XI or XII asking.*
*But it's the same dread I feel from competing with people like them that allows me to remain calm here and now.*
*Compared to them, she looks like your average woman. Slender and pretty, although you can tell she looks overtired. There's no doubt she's been getting little sleep.*
*She's wearing what I believe is a shawl atop a hospital gown.*
Keiko: "Tell me! What's your cause of death? What's your regret?"
*My silence makes her all the more agitated.*
Keiko: "Was it suicide? An illness? School? Love? Answer me!"
Rinka: "You need to calm down!"
*My patience starts to wear thin, which causes me to place my hands on her shoulders and shove her away from me.*
*I must've pushed her a bit too hard, since she stumbles backward.*
*She falls and lands on the hard concrete.*

*Their instinctual fear of him had taken over. Not even a gun would make them feel as though they stood on equal footing with him.*

*It's neither too close nor too far from the city.*
*Should everything check out over the next few days, he would use it as his base of operations.*

*Alan lets his thoughts slip out as he stares at the hotel room ceiling.*
*Two hours after I begin reading, I've made it through another fifth of the diary, I'd guess.*

*It had a leisurely attitude and seemed to be more attached to Dianna than Linda.*

*They called the cat Leo, which is pretty similar to Lethe.*

*Speak of the devil. It's Lethe.*
Rinka: "Hey, you should watch out for broken glass. You haven't walked on some already, have you?"
Lethe: "Meow."
*I try to approach, but Lethe runs off. Must've sensed something annoying was about to happen.*
*I assume it's fine if it can still sprint like that.*
*Following that, I close the diary and head back to my room.*
*Once in bed, I start to think about what I should do from here on out.*
*Let's put things into perspective. I have three main concerns at the moment.*
*First and most importantly: finding a means for both Miharu and me to survive.*
*I've yet to reach a conclusion, but I'm sure that figuring out the mysteries behind Divine Selection itself is the right approach.*

*This is a difficult one as well, especially when I don't understand his goal.*

Rinka: "Morning, Mao."

*Not to brag, but I haven't studied in the slightest ever since midterms.*
*Midterms weren't much of an issue for me since they happened soon after Divine Selection began, but the same can't be said for finals.*
*I actually considered using my card book to cheat my way through the English exam at least, but only total losers cheat.*

*That's when I receive a text message. You're not technically allowed to mess with your phone on campus, but I'll break that rule today.*

*I'll keep reading the diary as usual, but I guess I can avoid failing if I use the time I normally would on the store for studying.*

*Not like I can blame her. Her upperclassman is acting pretty pathetic.*

*I used to study with Mao a lot during our first year, but we normally ended up just chatting.*

Naomi: "I knew you could do it! You've earned a little break now."

*It was supposed to happen at the one-hour mark, but I couldn't bring myself to mention it when the time came.*
*Knowing her, she probably didn't want to interrupt me because she thought I was focused. Equally admirable and depressing, considering that wasn't the case at all.*

Naomi: "I should probably get going now."

*She can't stop herself from smiling after learning just how much Rinka dislikes studying. It has no effect on her impression of Rinka, but seeing this side of her has been a nice surprise.*
*To Naomi, the day was endless fun.*
*What's more, a certain desire has continued to blossom within her as the days have gone by.*
*The desire for things to continue like this. For her memories of these days to remain intact.*

*Numeral XII in Divine Selection. One of the four remaining participants.*

*The hospital...?*

*I'm certain I would've hesitated to elect him had he given me a proper answer, regardless of what it was.*

*She had no issue interacting with anyone who talked to her, and didn't find herself being ignored if she tried to engage others.*
*She never hung out with any of them after school or had lunch with them, though.*
*It wasn't particularly unusual at that stage of one's life.*
*Mao had already accepted that she didn't mind being alone, though.*
Mao: "So boring..."
*They'd all participate in class the same way.*
*They'd all wear the same things based on whatever they saw in magazines.*
*They'd all eat the same things based on places they saw on TV.*
*Mao found herself bored to death by the groupthink that surrounded her.*
*Why didn't they prioritize things they were personally invested in?*
*She had her reasons for thinking this way.*
*Nobody wanted to make their personal interests known. They were afraid of being different. That truth annoyed Mao. Perhaps she even hated them for it.*
*She made it a point not to use social media, either.*
*Only superficial thoughts and trivial woes got posted on there.*
*None of it mattered to her.*
*Instead, Mao looked toward the future. Toward the day she would finally enter high school.*
*She would be able to get a job then, allowing her to interact with those outside her school.*
*There were bound to be people she didn't dislike out there. That's what she believed.*
Mao: "Ugh..."
*Another day of coming to and leaving school on her own. That was the plan, but some of her classmates prevented that ideal scenario of hers from taking place.*
*It was a trio who found themselves in the upper echelon of the class's ranks due to their looks.*
*"Hey, do you know Miharu?"*
*They were in the same class, so of course Mao knew of her existence.*
*Mishima Miharu.*
*She was attending Amecha on a scholarship. Her mature looks were enough to catch the eyes of the entertainment business, leading to her being scouted a number of times.*
*Mao could tell what was coming next based on the question and their expressions.*
*"Doesn't she piss you off?"*
Mao: "I knew it."
*They looked shocked by her exclamation, but Mao told them not to read into it.*
*The situation at hand was a simple one.*
*Miharu's presence annoyed the trio, thus they wanted the rest of the class to ignore her as a result.*
*Mao was almost impressed by their ability to say that, despite there being an adult present in the room.*
Mao: "Leave me out of it."
*Giving a neutral response was Mao's way of handling such situations.*
*She wouldn't take part, but she wouldn't get in their way. She would simply keep a safe distance.*
*"Cold as ever, huh? Not like you ever talked to her in the first place though, so I guess that's fine."*
*After saying that, they gave up on their attempt to drag her in.*
*They were right, though. Mao never once approached or had been approached by Miharu.*
*Things would work out the way they wanted without her having to do anything.*
Mao: "Cold, huh..."
*It served as a lesson about how her classmates viewed her.*
*Her refusal to go along with their proposition meant she was cold.*
*Mao figured that they would've been willing to let her into their special circle had she accepted.*
*But at the same time, she couldn't understand why they held their own status in such high esteem. They weren't anyone special — just members of an irrelevant class at an irrelevant school in an irrelevant city.*
Mao: "Talk about pathetic."
*Mao rested her chin on her hands, clearly awestruck by their attitude.*
*At that moment, a thought came to her.*
*Just what sort of person was Mishima Miharu, anyway?*
*She must be different if her classmates were trying to get everyone to ignore her.*
*Perhaps it was a bit too early to seek company outside of school.*
*That made her take immediate action.*
Mao: "Hey. Wanna eat lunch on the roof together?"
*Mao walked right over to Miharu's seat and invited her.*
*Her classmates looked on in shock, but she made it a point to ignore them.*
*That only led to them receiving more attention, however.*
Miharu: "And what would I stand to gain from doing so? Sounds like nothing to me."
*Miharu's gaze remained focused on her textbook. Her tone was composed, yet firm.*
*Mao's thought process shut down for a moment, causing her face to burn a bright red.*
*Out of all the possible outcomes, she never expected that to happen.*
*She returned to her seat as the rest of the class giggled at her expense.*
*They weren't the only ones, though. Mao was smiling, too.*
*Perfect.*
*She'd faced a situation that she failed to anticipate. That interested her greatly.*
*Oguma Mao had all the prospects in the world during her elementary school days.*
*She got full marks on every exam she took.*
*As a result, her parents sent her to cram school to see how far she could go. She was recommended to take the entrance exams for middle school almost immediately.*
*The Oguma family was financially stable.*
*Those around Mao told her to study hard, and so she did.*
*She had the potential to enter some of the best schools in the country. Her parents truly believed this.*
*Much like most children would realize, though, days spent studying came at the cost of other activities.*
*That realization served as the trigger.*
*Mao began to put off studying were she to be invited out by friends, or if there was something she wanted to watch on TV.*
*She learned how to say no to things she didn't want to do.*
*Her perception of others changed as a result.*
*"Why do people keep doing things they don't want to?"*
*Mao was able to enter Amecha despite her new point of view.*
*Her parents and cram school teachers did not rejoice, though. This was a step down compared to what she was capable of.*
*An odd reaction, considering there were very few schools that stood above Amecha.*
*It would be some time until she came to understand that those expectations were no different from placing a burden on her, though.*
*In that sense, her attitude was mostly in line with the rebellious attitude of most teens.*
Mao: "Got a sec?"
*Mao approached Miharu on their way home.*
*Her response to being asked to ignore Miharu may have been cold, but Mao wasn't like that with everyone. She had little issue engaging in small talk with others.*
*That's why she found Miharu's previous reaction so interesting.*
*Being considered annoying or hated didn't matter.*
*All she wanted was to get to know Miharu better.*
Miharu: "Sorry, but I don't. I'm in a bit of a hurry right now."
*A response that Mao more or less expected.*
*She didn't push, though, opting instead to laugh and watch as Miharu walked off.*
*A few days later, their relationship had made no progress whatsoever.*
*Mao struggled to judge the right way to interact with others at this point in her life.*
*That's why she simply pressed on with talking to Miharu at any given moment.*
*Miharu continued to give her the cold shoulder in response.*
Mao: "But..."
*A certain question came to Mao over the last few days.*
Mao: "Why doesn't she ignore me completely?"
*Ignoring someone who's annoying seemed like the appropriate course of action to Mao.*
*Now she had to know why she wasn't being ignored.*
*A certain rumor had begun to spread around that time.*
*It was that Miharu had been slitting her wrists.*
*Self-harm wasn't all too rare among middle school students at all-girls schools, judging by statistics alone.*
*Mao herself had read that one in eleven committed it.*
*However, it was a rarity at Amecha. While technically a good thing, it worked against Miharu.*

*She may have come to realize why they referred to Miharu as a "freak" eventually.*

Mao: "It's her body. Can't she do what she wants with it?"
*There wasn't a hint of displeasure in her tone.*
*Her classmates reacted with absolute shock.*

*As such, the plan would serve no purpose.*
*Mao's refusal to align with them yesterday resulted in her becoming their new target, though.*
*Mao was never good friends with them in the first place, but she also didn't try to build a wall between herself and them like Miharu.*
*"She had the gall to defy us, so let's make her pay."*
*Their thought process was clear as day.*
*Miharu may have put a wall between them whenever Mao approached her, but she never ignored her, either.*
*They must have thought it would be thrilling to see Mao's reaction to being ignored out of nowhere.*
Miharu: "So I ignored them instead. The look on their faces when I did was quite something."
*After finishing her statement, Miharu made her way back to class.*
*An unusual feeling sprouted within Mao upon seeing Miharu's almost gallant figure.*
*Once in class and seated, the usual suspects approached her once more.*
*"So you'll never believe what I heard about Miharu..."*
*That's how the conversation began.*
*Mao couldn't help but be impressed by their ability to approach her right after suggesting to others that they ignore her.*
*Not that they would admit that to her, of course. How convenient that they only mentioned how Miharu ignored them.*
*They were clearly frustrated over it. Simply ignoring Miharu wasn't enough now — they wanted to bully her.*
Mao: "Gah, whatever! I don't care!"
*Unable to bear it any longer, Mao raised her arms and shouted her thoughts.*
*Needless to say, her classmates were taken aback.*
Mao: "Listen up. Don't bug me with this stuff."
Mao: "If you wanna ignore me, go ahead. Just stop dragging me into all your games."
*She gave them a taunting wink when she finished.*
*They were less than pleased with this, to the point where they walked off without another word.*
Mao: "Boy, that felt good."
*She stretched and proceeded to spend her day as usual.*
*It took a bit more time following that for Mao and Miharu to start having lunch together.*
*Nothing special happened during that time. They became closer by nature of the attitude shown to them by the rest of the class.*
*As for the usual suspects, one was kicked out of the group after her secret social network account was exposed. Another group took advantage of that and forced themselves to the uppermost echelon. That led to a number of changes in the classroom landscape.*
*The rest of the class, who once feared becoming a target of their bullying, soon stopped caring altogether.*
*Mao once again became a person who most people could approach, while most stayed away from Miharu. In other words, things had returned to normal.*
*One thing had changed, however.*
*Mao and Miharu had gone from strangers to friends.*
Miharu: "Hey, Mao."
Mao: "What's up, Miharun?"
Miharu: "We don't need to pretend that we like things, do we?"
Mao: "That's how I feel about it."
*Mao responded and let out a sigh.*
